title: Voyager plugin manifest
description: A declarative Voyager plugin (plugin.json). Hand-written to mirror the gates, which are the authority: this schema is editor tooling. A bundled plugin goes through `bun run plugin:check <dir>` (the site it ships under, the primitives this build carries, translation completeness). A local plugin goes through the popup import; `npx create-voyager-plugin check <dir>` runs the same checks offline, including the local-only rules no schema can express: `matches` must stay inside a site Voyager supports, every semantic key must be declared by every matched site, Gemini and AI Studio take no `theme` and no `native` op, and settings are boolean, number or select only. Unknown top-level keys are ignored rather than rejected, exactly as the validators ignore them.

$schema.description: This schema's URL, so editors validate the file as you type.

id.description: Globally unique, reverse-dotted (e.g. `voyager.claude-reading-width`). A local plugin is stored as `local.<id>`; write the id without that prefix.

name.description: Display name: English for a bundled plugin, any language for a local one.

description.description: One-liner shown in the popup: English for a bundled plugin, any language for a local one.

category.description: Classification. The known set is render-fix, theme, layout, readability, productivity, integration, other; any string is accepted so third parties are not boxed in.

engine.description: Semver range the plugin needs of the host engine: `*`, an exact `x.y.z`, or `>=x.y.z`. Repository contributors may use `>=next` for an unreleased primitive or capability; catalog publishing resolves it to a concrete version. Local imports require a concrete version. A plugin that invokes a primitive must set a floor at or above that primitive's `sinceEngine`; settings tokens in native params also require engine 1.8.0 or later. These floors make an older Voyager say "update Voyager" instead of silently misinterpreting params or reporting a missing handler.

tier.description: `declarative` ships only data (CSS + JSON) interpreted by the bundled engine. `scripted` is reserved for a later advanced tier with no runtime yet; a scripted plugin is skipped entirely.

matches.description: URL match patterns the plugin applies to. A bundled plugin must stay inside the matches of the site it ships under, a local plugin inside the matches of a site Voyager supports. The gates enforce that; this schema cannot.

brand.description: Accent for Voyager's own UI on the matched site(s); overrides the site adapter's brandColor. Hex only — the value is concatenated into a CSS `color-mix(...)` expression.

theme.description: Optional brand accent contributed for the matched site(s). Not allowed on Gemini or AI Studio.

format.description: Manifest format major. Absent means 1; published host catalogs always carry it.

requires.description: What the plugin needs from the host beyond the engine range. A miss disables the plugin with a reason (needs-form-factor / needs-handler / needs-semantic) instead of hiding it.

handlers.description: Primitive names the plugin invokes. Optional: a `native` op already implies its handler, so list one only to state the dependency explicitly.

semantic.description: Semantic selector keys the plugin expects its site adapter to define (see site.schema.json). Every matched site must declare each one.

formFactors.description: Device classes the plugin runs on. Absent means desktop and mobile. ["desktop"] keeps a plugin that cannot work on a phone off there: on an Android phone it reports needs-form-factor, its switch disabled with a reason and the user's choice kept. Builds older than this key ignore it and run the plugin everywhere, so it needs no engine floor.

changelog.description: One line describing this version, shown in the popup. When set, every locale in `i18n` needs a translated `changelog` too.

i18n.description: Localized metadata keyed by app language code. `en` is not needed — the top-level fields are the English copy, and every field falls back to them individually. `plugin:check` requires name and description (plus changelog and every setting label, when present) for ar, es, fr, ja, ko, pt, ru, zh and zh_TW in a bundled plugin; a local plugin may leave `i18n` out.

hexColor.description: A strict hex literal (3, 4, 6 or 8 digits), e.g. `#d97757`.

contributions.description: Everything the plugin adds to the page. New capabilities arrive as new keys here — a plugin never runs code of its own.

settings.description: User-configurable settings, rendered by the popup. A `{{key}}` token in CSS text, a setStyle value, a setAttribute value or a native params string is replaced with the current value (the default until the user changes it). Native params tokens require engine 1.8.0 or later. A local plugin may use boolean, number and select settings only: the popup has no control for string or color yet.

styleContribution.description: CSS injected as a <style> element. Authors write `{ "file": "style.css" }`; the build (or the popup's Import files) inlines it as `{ "css": "…" }`, which is the form published catalogs carry. Scope rules under the plugin's own `gv-` classes; `{{key}}` setting tokens are substituted. CSS may not load anything: no `@import`, `image-set()`, `image()`, `cross-fade()` or `src()`, and `url()` only with a `#fragment` or a raster-image `data:` URI (png, jpeg, gif, webp, avif, bmp, ico; never SVG).

file.description: Path to a .css file beside plugin.json. Relative, no `..`, no query or fragment.

source.description: The style file the CSS was inlined from. Written by the build.

selectorRef.description: Where an operation applies: a bare CSS selector string (sugar for `{"kind":"css"}`), an explicit css ref, or a semantic key the site adapter maps to a site-specific selector. Prefer semantic keys — a site redesign is then a one-file adapter fix.

key.description: A semantic key every matched site declares (see site.schema.json).

domOperation.description: One reversible DOM operation interpreted by the bundled engine.

className.description: Exactly one class name starting with `gv-`, conventionally `gv-plugin-<plugin>`. Style it in `contributes.styles`.

name.description: An inert attribute: data-*, aria-*, or one of title, role, lang, dir, hidden, tabindex, draggable, spellcheck, translate, style. Never href, src, on*, class or id.

value.description: May not contain an external URL; a `style` value follows the setStyle rules. `{{key}}` setting tokens are substituted.

styles.description: CSS property → value, custom properties included. Anything that loads (a url() other than a raster-image data: URI or #fragment, image-set(), …) is rejected. `{{key}}` setting tokens are substituted.

oneOf.title: native
oneOf.description: Invoke a first-party primitive by name. `params` is configuration, never instructions; the primitive validates its own params. The engine floor must clear the primitive's sinceEngine, and every matched site must declare the semantic keys it reads: the gates enforce both. On Gemini or AI Studio, local native ops must belong to a plugin-owned public feature. Consumer-Gemini turnNavigator requires literal dataBackend: shared, native identity and consumer-only matches; the local gate and runtime enforce this policy.

handler.description: A primitive this Voyager build ships; the write-voyager-plugin skill lists each one with its params.

params.description: Plain JSON configuration: primitives, arrays and objects of those, at most 4 levels deep, 50 keys or entries per level and 2000 chars per string. String values recursively support {{settingKey}} tokens; parameter names and object keys stay literal. A whole-value token preserves the setting's number, boolean or string type; embedded tokens produce a string. Expansion runs once, so tokens inside setting values remain literal. Every referenced key must exist in contributes.settings and its type must fit the primitive contract wherever statically knowable. Loading checks substituted defaults; each activation substitutes resolved stored values and runs the primitive's validateParams, skipping an invalid op through the same diagnostic path as invalid static params. Settings changes serialize disposal and reactivation for templated ops; static params keep in-place updates. Requires engine 1.8.0 or later, plus any higher primitive/param floor; catalog authors use >=next while the capability is unreleased, local imports use concrete versions.

localization.description: One locale's copy. Every field is optional and falls back to the English original on its own.
